text: . Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, the mantra of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ had instilled new self-confidence among the poor, enabling crores of people to overcome poverty. Mr Modi was addressing the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme at Gadchiroli in Maharashtra, through video conferencing as part of the nationwide celebrations marking the 151st birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.The Prime Minister said the government has devoted special attention and resources to the most backward tribal regions, which lacked basic amenities. He said over one lakh crore rupees had been allocated for the PM-JANMAN Yojana and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan.Mr Modi said Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, which was first observed on 15th November 2021, has now become a national celebration. He said there was a time when many national occasions and festivals were viewed through a foreign perspective, but today, India is remembering its heritage, history and heroes with a sense of pride and self-respect. He described this as a significant shift in the country’s national consciousness.The Prime Minister said two major achievements of the country are being widely discussed. He said nearly 50 crore people have overcome extreme poverty, while the country has also made significant progress in eliminating Naxalism and Maoist violence. Mr Modi said the government has placed special emphasis on regions that have lagged behind in development for a long time. Special campaigns have been launched across more than 100 Aspirational Districts and 500 Aspirational Blocks, including areas with significant tribal populations. He added that, under the PM Krishi Dhan-Dhaanya Yojana, special attention is being given to 100 districts that are lagging behind in the agricultural sector.Referring to a recent World Bank report stating that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of extreme poverty over the past 12 to 13 years, the Prime Minister described it as one of India’s major achievements since Independence. He said this progress was the result not of any single government but of the collective efforts of society, the hard work of citizens and targeted government initiatives, including schemes and measures for tribal welfare.Mr Modi also interacted with selected tribal beneficiaries during the programme.On the occasion, the Prime Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 246 development projects worth around three thousand crore rupees. The projects aim to strengthen education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country. He inaugurated 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multipurpose Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN). These centres will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities.The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools and 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs). In addition, he inaugurated and launched several other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, and laid the foundation stones for 42 projects under the two initiatives.Mr Modi also inaugurated the Tribal Research Institute building at Itanagar in Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museum in Mizoram. These facilities aim to preserve and promote tribal culture and heritage.The programme marked the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, observed across the country from the 1st to the 15th of November.Union Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram and Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also addressed the gathering in Gadchiroli.

. The third day of Chhath Mahaparv is being celebrated with religious fervour and enthusiasm across the country. The ritual of Sandhya Arghya was performed this evening, during which lakhs of devotees offered Arghya to the setting Sun.As part of the ritual, devotees stand in rivers, ponds and other water bodies and offer water, milk and prayers to the setting Sun, seeking blessings for the health, prosperity and well-being of their families.The four-day festival will conclude tomorrow morning with the ritual of Usha Arghya, during which devotees will offer prayers to the rising Sun. This marks the final ritual of Chhath Puja, following which devotees will break their nearly 36-hour-long fast.President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have extended greetings to the people on the occasion.

. The International Cricket Council (ICC) Board has approved the windows for major men’s events until 2035, confirming that India will host the 2029 Champions Trophy and co-host the 2031 ODI World Cup with Bangladesh.The 2029 Champions Trophy will be held in India from 9th to 28th of October, while the 2031 ODI World Cup will take place from 9th October to 23rd November, jointly hosted by India and Bangladesh.The ICC also announced the dates for tournaments beyond 2031, although the host nations are yet to be confirmed. The schedule covers major events from the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand to the 2035 ODI World Cup.The 2028 T20 World Cup will run from October 12 to  November 12. The next edition will be held in 2030, with England, Scotland and Ireland jointly hosting the tournament. The 2032 and 2034 editions are also scheduled, but their venues are yet to be announced.Meanwhile, the World Test Championship (WTC) Final will continue to be held every two years in June until 2035. England will host the 2029 and 2031 finals, while the hosts for the 2033 and 2035 editions are yet to be decided.

. SpaceX has successfully caught the upper stage of its massive Starship rocket using mechanical arms at its launch tower in Texas, marking a major milestone in the company’s efforts to develop a fully reusable launch system.The historic recovery took place yesterday at the company’s Starbase facility, following its 15th test flight. The spacecraft completed 14 orbits around Earth before returning to the launch tower, where it was caught by mechanical arms, popularly known as ‘chopsticks’.However, the mission faced a setback during its initial phase on Friday, when the rocket’s booster failed to return for a planned recovery. It was diverted for a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico but exploded before reaching the water.The test marked the first attempt by SpaceX to catch both the booster and upper stage of Starship during a single mission.The flight also saw the deployment of 26 Starlink Version 3 satellites into orbit, adding to the company’s satellite internet network, which already has more than 11,000 satellites in low Earth orbit. The company also envisions using Starship for future missions to Mars.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has accused Iran of fuelling major conflicts across the Middle East, describing Tehran’s regional ambitions as an extraordinary historic danger.Addressing a gathering in Washington, Rubio cited the Houthis, Hezbollah and Shia militias as examples of Iranian influence. Meanwhile, tensions have intensified following reports of oil tankers catching fire after striking naval mines in and around the Strait of Hormuz.Iran’s Navy has blamed vessels for entering restricted waters without coordination and warned shipping operators against violating maritime restrictions. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf has expressed readiness for negotiations with Washington, subject to seven conditions, while rejecting prolonged uncertainty between war and peace.

. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani has said that Operation Sindoor, which was launched last year following the Pahalagam terror attack, demonstrated that the Indian Armed Forces has the capability to fight wars with indigenous weapons. He was speaking at a National Security Summit organised by a private news agency in New Delhi.The CDS said that Operation Sindoor is a very good example of joint planning and multi-domain integration between the three Services. General Subramani said that indigenous air defence systems like Akash succeeded in deterring Pakistani aerial attacks.He highlighted that the country has succeeded in establishing the process of expanding its defence industrial base. He said that most of its contracts are being given to domestic manufacturers and its exports have touched 38 thousand crores to over 80 countries in the world last year.Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit said that self-reliance in the country’s defence system is not just an industrial goal but an operational requirement. Air Chief said that the country’s defence production has reached an all-time high of 1.78 lakh crore rupees in financial year 2025-26 which is 15.5 percent more than the previous year.

. India’s forex reserves have recorded an increase of 2.49 billion to reach 719.547 billion dollars during the week ended 6th November 2026. According to an official press release issued by the Reserve Bank, the foreign currency assets, a major component of the reserves, spiked by 232 million dollars to 591.350  billion dollars.In the previous reporting week, the reserves had dropped by 2.691 billion dollars to 717.056 billion dollars.As per the statement, gold reserves jumped by 2.205 billion dollars to 104.796 billion dollars. The Special Drawing Rights – SDRs also went up by 52 million dollars to 18.610  billion dollars and India’s reserve position with the IMF also recorded a rise  of 1 million dollars to 4.791   billion dollars at the end of the reporting week.

. Indian Coast Guard in association with the Department of Border Management, Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), is organising a two-day National Level Coastal Security Seminar, ‘Sagar Suraksha 2026’, in Kolkata from 16 to 17 Nov 2026. Anchored on the theme “Comprehensive Approach to Coastal Security:Strengthening Stakeholder Participation and Community Engagement”, the seminar underscores the nation’s unwavering commitment towards fortifying an integrated and resilient coastal security architecture.The event will be inaugurated by Shri Bishal Lama, Hon’ble Minister of State for Home and Hill Affairs, Government of West Bengal.The conclave will bring together senior leadership and key representatives from coastal States and Union Territories, Central Ministries, the Armed Forces, Central Armed Police Forces, and allied maritime agencies.Participants will engage in focused deliberations on operational challenges, critical vulnerabilities, and emerging threat dimensions across the maritime domain. ‘Sagar Suraksha 2026’ will serve as a premier strategic platform to share operational best practices and forge a synergised response mechanism against evolving threats to India’s coastal and maritime interests.The deliberations are aimed at generating actionable policy perspectives, enhancing inter-agency synergy, and advancing a unified national approach toward securing India’s coastline as an impregnable maritime frontier.

. US stock markets ended on a mixed note yesterday. The Nasdaq Composite shed 0.9 per cent, the S&P 500 dropped 0.4 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average eked out a gain of 0.1 per cent. All three major Wall Street indices posted gains for the week. The S&P surged 2.5 per cent, the Nasdaq rose 2.3 per cent and the Dow climbed 2.1 per cent.On the economic front, the US Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 6.5 percent year-on-year in October, marking its sharpest annual increase since November 2022, according to data released by the US Department of Labour.Meanwhile, comments from multiple ⁠Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

. Tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia have escalated, with both neighbouring countries accusing each other of supporting armed groups fighting within their territories.Sudan’s military alleges that Ethiopia is providing camps and logistical support to the Rapid Support Forces, or RSF, paramilitary group.Ethiopia, meanwhile, accused Sudan of backing rebels in its northern Tigray region, where fighting has recently resumed. The diplomatic row intensified after Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consular staff and ordered the closure of its consulate in Asosa.The escalating tensions are raising fears of a wider regional conflict, amid competing international alliances, disputes over the Nile River dam and contested border territories.

. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 21 paise to trade at Rs 94. 25 against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.23 in intra-day trade.

. Today is the National Press Day. The day reaffirms the vital role of a free, responsible, and ethical press in strengthening the Nation’s democracy.The day marks the establishment of the Press Council of India, PCI which began its operations on this day in 1966. Established as an independent body, the PCI’s primary role is to ensure that the press maintains high standards of journalism while remaining free from external influences.This year the theme of the National Press Day Celebration is “Journalism: Populist or Responsible.Akashvani correspondent reports that National Press Day serves as an important reminder of the vital role that the press plays in shaping the country’s democracy.Since its establishment, the Press Council of India has worked tirelessly to uphold press freedom, maintain journalistic standards, and address challenges facing the media. From tackling issues like media ethics and press safety to adapting to the digital age, the Council continues to guide and support the media in its mission to inform, educate, and empower the public.National Press Day not only celebrates the achievements of the press but also reinforces the responsibility it carries in building a more informed and transparent society, ensuring that the future of journalism remains strong, free, and responsible.Meanwhile, Nagaland Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio has extended greetings to the press and media fraternity on the occasion of National Press Day.In a social media post on X, the Chief Minister said the role of the media in keeping society informed, amplifying voices and holding institutions accountable is indispensable to a healthy democracy.Mr Rio urged the media fraternity to continue upholding press freedom, responsible journalism and public trust. On the occasion, press clubs across Nagaland are organising various programmes to mark National Press Day.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India recorded an all-time high in exports, reaching nearly 90 billion dollars in October this year.Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the India International Trade Fair (IITF) in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said the export figure of October comprised around 50 billion dollars in merchandise exports and 40 billion dollars in services exports. He further informed that India’s cumulative exports during the first seven months of the current financial year, up to October, has reached 570 billion dollars. Expressing confidence in the country’s export performance, the Minister said India is well on course to achieve its one-trillion-dollar export target this year.Mr Goyal also expressed confidence that India’s international trade will register growth of 15 to 16 per cent during the current year, despite ongoing conflicts and global uncertainties. He said the country’s performance reflects the resilience of its economy, the confidence of its exporters and India’s ability to overcome global challenges with determination and self-respect.Highlighting the strength of India’s domestic economy, Mr Goyal referred to the strong business activity witnessed during the recent festive season, particularly around Diwali. He said markets across the country recorded robust consumer demand and increased business activity. The Minister also pointed out that GST collections in October touched an all-time high for the month. He expressed confidence that November would also see record collections, reflecting the continued momentum of economic activity across the country. Referring to India’s long-term economic ambitions, Mr Goyal said the country, currently a four-trillion-dollar economy, aspires to become a 30-trillion-dollar economy by 2047.Speaking about the India International Trade Fair, the Minister said, the event has emerged as an important platform bringing together states, businesses, products and India’s diverse capabilities under one roof. He announced that the India Trade Promotion Organisation would take the IITF platform to international destinations by organising several overseas trade fairs, covering both specific sectors and multiple industries. These initiatives will provide Indian manufacturers, service providers and start-ups with opportunities to showcase their capabilities and connect with buyers and markets across the world, including developed economies. Mr Goyal added that the 45th edition of IITF had moved beyond incremental improvements, marking a significant step towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.The annual India International Trade Fair, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, begins in New Delhi today. It brings together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad. The theme of this year’s fair is ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. A total of 32 States and Union Territories will participate in the 14-day event, showcasing their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, cultural heritage, tourism potential and development initiatives. The fair will provide a major platform for businesses, entrepreneurs and participating states to promote their products, explore new opportunities and strengthen domestic as well as international trade ties.

. Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia have announced their withdrawal from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait in the southern Red Sea, leaving the key shipping gateway under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement.Yemen’s military said troops were being redeployed from the Dhubab Airport and Bab al-Mandab area to strengthen front lines and defend the interim capital, Aden.The withdrawal ends a weeks-long offensive to regain control of the territory after the Houthis seized parts of the region, including Perim Island at the southern entrance to the Red Sea and the strategic port city of Mokha, in September.Houthi-run media reported on Sunday that the group had taken control of the area. Saudi Arabia has not yet commented on the reported withdrawal.The development has raised concerns over international shipping and global oil supplies. Bab al-Mandab connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea making it one of the world’s most important maritime trade routes.Ships passing through the strait can access the Suez Canal, which links the Red Sea with the Mediterranean.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has left on a two-day visit to the Philippines. During the visit, Prime Minister Modi will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS), which is being hosted tomorrow by the Philippines as the ASEAN Chair for 2026.India-ASEAN relations are a central pillar of India’s Act East Policy and our vision for the Indo-Pacific. The visit comes as India and ASEAN are celebrating 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, and will commemorate 35 years of Dialogue Relations and five years of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2027.The ASEAN-India Summit will review progress in the implementation of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the ASEAN-India Plan of Action 2026-2030, and chart the future direction of cooperation.The East Asia Summit will provide an opportunity to exchange views on matters of regional and global importance with ASEAN and other participating countries.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has paid tributes to revolutionary and freedom fighter Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha. In a social media post, Mr Singh said that Kartar Singh Sarabha sacrificed his life for the country’s independence at just 19 years of age.The Defence Minister added that the indomitable courage and devotion of Kartar Singh Sarabha to the motherland will always be remembered and will continue to inspire future generations..

. Most Asian stock markets ended in negative territory today. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng shed 1.6 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi as well as Singapore’s Strait Times index lost nearly one per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite fell 0.6 per cent. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained over half a per cent and Taiwan’s Taiex rose 1.4 per cent.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.1 per cent, while Germany’s DAX eked out a marginal gain, when reports last came in.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that the Indian community in Egypt is a living bridge between the two countries, highlighting its role in strengthening economic, cultural and people-to-people ties.Addressing an Indian community event organised by the Indian Community Association in Egypt, Mr Goyal said bilateral trade, currently worth around 6.5 billion dollars, represents only the beginning of the partnership between the two countries. He also highlighted the contribution of nearly 70 Indian companies operating in Egypt, with investments exceeding 5 billion dollars and generating direct and indirect employment for Egyptians.Mr Goyal arrived in Cairo yesterday on a two-day visit to strengthen India-Egypt ties and expand trade, investment and industrial cooperation. A delegation of more than 130 business leaders and start-ups is accompanying him.The visit includes the seventh India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting, scheduled for today, along with a Joint Business Council meeting and a business forum. Mr Goyal will also meet senior Egyptian ministers, business leaders and officials of the African Export-Import Bank.During the visit, he paid tribute to Indian soldiers at Cairo’s Heliopolis War Cemetery, where 3,727 Indian soldiers are commemorated.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, yesterday. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs.Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named Player of the Match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded Player of the Tournament.Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led the bowling attack, claiming four wickets.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have congratulated the Indian team on its victory in the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup 2026.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. India and Egypt today agreed to work towards finalising the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a proposed bilateral trade agreement to strengthen economic ties between the two countries. At the 7th India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting in Cairo, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said, the two countries could enhance cooperation in several sectors, including pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering and automobiles, agriculture, digitisation, fintech and museums.Highlighting opportunities for cooperation in the fintech sector, Mr Goyal said the central banks of both countries were working to promote trade in local currencies. He also proposed linking India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with Egypt’s digital payment systems. The Minister said a joint team from both countries would work in a time-bound manner to finalise the Terms of Reference for the proposed trade agreement. He said the agreement could take bilateral economic relations to a new level by expanding trade and investment and promoting a more comprehensive partnership across various sectors, including education. The Egyptian delegation was led by Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt.Mr Goyal arrived in Cairo yesterday on a two-day visit aimed at strengthening India-Egypt relations and expanding trade, investment and industrial cooperation. A delegation of more than 130 business leaders and start-ups is accompanying him.

. The NSE International Exchange (NSEIX), NSE’s global investment platform, has announced the expansion of its global investment offerings into seven key European markets through its GIFT City-based entity. The expansion increases Indian investors’ access to European-listed securities and Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs).NSEIX Global Access IFSC Limited (NSEIXGA), India’s first entity registered as a Global Access Provider under the regulatory framework of the International Financial Services Centres Authority, said in a statement that the expanded investment universe includes more than 11,500 securities, including over 8,200 UCITS ETFs across the European markets, including France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.A key feature of the new offering is access to UCITS ETFs, which combine the benefits of exchange-traded investment products with an established European regulatory framework. These ETFs provide access to a wide range of global indices, markets, sectors, themes and asset classes, offering investors an alternative to investing in individual securities. UCITS ETFs also offer distinct tax advantages, further enhancing their appeal as an option for globally diversified investments.With this addition, investors will have access to a broader range of international investment products beyond the platform’s existing offerings in the US market. The expansion aims to cater to growing investor interest in international markets by providing access to a wider range of investment opportunities through a single integrated account.

. The third day of Chhath Puja is being celebrated across Nepal with religious fervour and devotion, particularly in the Tarai-Madhes region and the Kathmandu Valley. The ritual of Sandhya Arghya was performed this evening with devotees gathered at riverbanks, ponds and other water bodies to offer prayers to the setting Sun. In the Kathmandu Valley, special arrangements were made at several locations, including Gaurighat, Guhyeshwori and Kamal Pokhari, where large numbers of devotees gathered to perform traditional rituals. Carrying bamboo baskets filled with fruits, sugarcane, thekua and other traditional offerings, devotees stood in water and offered Arghya to the setting Sun. Women observing the fast prayed for the health, prosperity and well-being of their families.The four-day Chhath Puja is one of the most important festivals in Nepal’s Tarai-Madhes region and has also gained popularity in the Kathmandu Valley and other parts of the country. The festival will conclude tomorrow morning with Usha Arghya, when devotees will offer prayers to the rising Sun. They will break their 36-hour long fast following the ritual.

. In Football, India registered a 2-1 victory over Bhutan in the semifinal of the SAFF Championship in Dhaka today. With this win India booked their place in the final and keeping their pursuit of a record-extending 10th title alive. Vishnu PV opened the scoring for India in the ninth minute, while captain Chinglensana Singh Konsham doubled the lead in the 27th minute. Kinzang Tashi Tobden’s scored only goal for Bhutan in the 48th minute. India will now face the winner of the other semifinal between Bangladesh and Pakistan in the final on November 17.

. Global crude oil prices declined for the second consecutive week. Brent crude January futures dropped 2.5 per cent to settle at 95 US dollars and 84 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude December futures also lost 2.5 per cent to end at 88 US dollars and 56 cents per barrel over the week.Despite easing prices, risks to oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz remained.Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said on a social media post that a deal ​with Iran was not necessary to end the war.

. In Badminton, India’s Lakshya Sen has stormed into the men’s singles final of the Kumamoto Masters Japan after defeating Indonesia’s sixth-seeded Alwi Farhan 21-12, 15-21, 21-11 in a thrilling three-game semifinal today. The 25-year-old Indian shuttler will now face Japan’s Koki Watanabe in the title clash tomorrow. Sen dominated the opening game, winning it 21-12. However, Farhan fought back to take the second game 21-15, forcing a decider. The Indian shuttler then produced a strong comeback in the deciding game, winning it convincingly 21-11 to seal his place in the final.

. Yemen’s Houthi armed forces have claimed responsibility for launching two ballistic missiles targeting King Khalid International Airport and a financial centre in Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh.In a statement posted on Social media, Houthi military spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree claimed that the strikes successfully hit their intended targets. Saudi Arabia had not immediately responded to the claims.The Houthis claimed to have fired six ballistic missiles at Saudi troop concentrations at the Qa’wa camp and nearby locations in Yemen’s Lahj Governorate.Saree alleged that the strikes targeted forces under Saudi officer Badr al-Harbi, causing dozens of casualties and destroying several vehicles. These claims could not be independently verified.Saree also alleged that Saudi warplanes carried out 75 airstrikes and missile attacks over the preceding 24 hours across Saada, Taiz, Lahj, Al-Jawf and Marib provinces, resulting in civilian casualties. He said the attacks involved F-15 and Typhoon aircraft operating from Khamis Mushait and Taif airbases, along with missile strikes launched from Najran.The Houthi spokesperson further claimed that the total number of Saudi-led airstrikes and missile attacks since the escalation began had reached 5,095. Rejecting Saudi reports that drones had been intercepted over Mecca and Medina, Saree called the claims fabricated, insisting that Houthi operations targeted only Saudi oil facilities and military bases.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Indian stock market extended its gaining streak for the third consecutive week, supported by strong foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows and better-than-expected corporate earnings. However, rising retail inflation, elevated US Treasury yields, rupee weakness and uncertainty surrounding the global monetary policy outlook limit the pace of gains.The 30-share Sensex at the Bombay Stock Exchange climbed 564 points, or 0.7 per cent, to close at 81 thousand 592. The National Stock Exchange Nifty 50 gained 114 points, or nearly half a per cent to end at 25 thousand and 144. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, Midcap 100 index soared 2.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index surged 3.6 per cent during the week.On the sectoral front, the Nifty PSU Bank index emerged as the top performer, surging 7.5 per cent over the week. The Nifty Media index advanced 5.2 per cent, while the Nifty Capital Markets index gained 3.8 per cent. In contrast, the Nifty IT index was the weakest performer among the major sectoral indices, declining 3.2 per cent, while the Nifty Cement index slipped 2.1 per cent.Investor wealth on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) witnessed a significant uptick this week, with the combined market capitalisation of all listed companies surging by over 7 lakh crore rupees.In the forex market, the Indian rupee depreciated by 34 paise this week to settle at 94 rupees and 25 paise against the US dollar.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games. The Games will be held across six cities in Telangana from 11th to 22nd of next month.Addressing the gathering, Dr Mandaviya said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and making sports an integral part of the country’s development vision. He said various sporting events, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of young people in sports.Speaking on the occasion, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said events such as the Khelo India Youth Games would help advance the Prime Minister’s vision of a Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat by encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse and other social challenges.Both Dr Mandaviya and Mr Reddy expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said around eight thousand athletes and participants are expected to take part in the Games. The 8th edition will feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. Minister of Foreign Affairs of Belarus Maxim Ryzhenkov has arrived in New Delhi on a four-day visit to India.The Ministry of External Affairs said that he will co-chair the 12th Meeting of the India-Belarus Intergovernmental Commission on Cooperation in the fields of Trade, Economy, Science, Technology and Culture with Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada today.He will also hold talks with Minister of State for External Affairs, Kirti Vardhan Singh, tomorrow.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal has moved north-northwestwards and intensified into a deep depression.The IMD said that the system is very likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal today. It is further expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal tomorrow.The Met Department has advised the fishermen not to venture into Andaman Sea, Southeast Bay of Bengal and along and off the Andaman and Nicobar Islands till tomorrow.The Weather Agency has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. IMD has also forecast dense fog conditions over Uttar Pradesh today.Meanwhile, air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 216 as of 7 AM today.

. Indian women’s hockey player and Olympian Lalremsiami Hmar today became the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive the prestigious Arjuna Award, adding another milestone to her trailblazing career.The 26-year-old was among 17 sportspersons selected for the Arjuna Award 2025 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports on August 18. President Droupadi Murmu formally presented the honour to her at a ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi today.Lalremsiami, who hailed from Kolasib in the northern part of Mizoram bordering Assam, took up hockey at a young age.Her talent was spotted by teachers Lallawmawmi, Lalrampari and Lalrothuami, who encouraged her to pursue the sport.Lalremsiami joined the state-run hockey academy at Thenzawl in 2011 at the age of 11, before moving to the National Hockey Academy in New Delhi in 2016.Lalremsiami made her national debut at the Junior Nehru Hockey Tournament in October 2011 and was later selected for India’s Under-18 team for the Asian Cup in 2016.She earned her first senior national team call-up in 2017 and was part of India’s Asia Cup-winning side that year.Since then, she has established herself as a key member of the Indian team, featuring in several major international tournaments, including the Tokyo Olympics 2020, where India finished fourth.She created history in 2018 by becoming the first sportsperson from Mizoram to win an Asian Games medal, helping India secure silver.Her commitment to the national team drew widespread admiration in 2019 when she chose to remain with the squad for the FIH Women’s Series in Japan despite the death of her father, Lalthansanga Zote.India won the tournament and secured qualification for the Tokyo Olympics, making Lalremsiami the first woman from Mizoram to compete at the Olympics.She followed in the footsteps of archer C. Lalremsanga, who represented India at the 1992 Barcelona and 1996 Atlanta Olympics.In 2020, Lalremsiami became the first Indian female hockey player to win the International Hockey Federation’s Women’s Rising Star of the Year award.Her list of achievements has since grown to include a bronze at the 2022 Asian Games, Asian Champions Trophy titles in 2023 and 2024, and gold at the 2026 Asian Games.The Mizoram government had earlier announced a cash reward of Rs 40 lakh each for Lalremsiami and fellow Mizo player Lalthantluangi for their contribution to India’s women’s hockey team that won gold at the Asian Games on October 2.The Arjuna Award now adds another distinction to Lalremsiami’s career, making her the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive one of the country’s highest honours for sporting achievement.

. Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas was celebrated acrossJharkhandtoday with reverence and enthusiasm, marking the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. A series of programmes were organised across the state to commemorate the occasion. These included a tribute ceremony at Khunti, the inauguration of new Eklavya Model Residential Schools in Gumla and the laying of the foundation stone for another school in Ranchi. The celebrations culminated in a grand Deepotsav this evening.InMadhya Pradesh,various programmes were organised to mark Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, commemorating the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The state-level celebration was held at Dahis in Dhar district. Governor Mangubhai Patel and Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav attended the programme and listened to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s virtual address. On the occasion, the Governor and the Chief Minister dedicated the Dahi Micro Irrigation Lift Project, constructed at a cost of over 1,353 crore rupees, to the people. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav said that the life and sacrifices of Bhagwan Birsa Munda inspire everyone to dedicate themselves to the service of the nation.Manipurjoined the rest of the country in celebrating Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas today, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Department of Tribal Affairs and Hills, Government of Manipur, organised the celebrations along with the inauguration of the State-Level Tribal Cultural Festival at the City Convention Centre in Imphal.During the programme in Manipur, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh presented prizes to the winners of the Tribal Lens Photo Competition and the Tribal Frames Manipur 2026 Film Awards, recognising their contributions to documenting and showcasing tribal life, culture and heritage.The festival, scheduled from today until the 18th of November, will feature cultural performances highlighting the rich traditions, heritage, art and identity of Manipur’s tribal communities. The Chief Minister also visited the exhibition stalls set up as part of the celebrations and inspected the displays.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated hosts New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth and final One Day International at Mount Maunganui to clinch the series 3-1. With this victory, India also ended New Zealand’s 11-series unbeaten streak at home.Put in to bat, India were bowled out for 209 in 42.1 overs. Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan were the top scorers, contributing 46 runs each. In reply, New Zealand, chasing a target of 210 runs, were bowled out for 187 in 48.1 overs. For India, Arshdeep Singh claimed three wickets, while Mohammed Siraj and Axar Patel took two wickets each. Arshdeep was named Player of the Match, while Gurnoor Brar was adjudged Player of the Series.

. In Football, India registered a 2-1 victory over Bhutan in the semifinal of the SAFF Championship in Dhaka yesterday. With this win India booked their place in the final and keeping their pursuit of a record-extending 10th title alive.Vishnu PV opened the scoring for India in the ninth minute, while captain Chinglensana Singh Konsham doubled the lead in the 27th minute. Kinzang Tashi Tobden’s scored only goal for Bhutan in the 48th minute.India will now face the winner of the other semifinal between Bangladesh and Pakistan in the final on Tuesday.

. In badminton, India’s Lakshya Sen clinched the men’s singles title at the Kumamoto Masters Japan, defeating Japan’s Koki Watanabe in a thrilling three-game final this morning.Lakshya fought back from a game down to win 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in one hour and four minutes. With this victory, he became the first Indian shuttler to win the tournament since its inception in 2023.This was Lakshya’s second consecutive BWF Super 500 title, following his triumph at the Hylo Open in Germany earlier this month. It was also his sixth BWF World Tour title and the first time he has won two Tour titles in a single season.The victory earned him 9,200 ranking points, boosting his chances of qualifying for the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou.

. The 49th ASEAN Summit began in Manila this morning, with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. calling for greater regional unity and collective action to address geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainties and security challenges.Addressing regional leaders during the opening ceremony, Marcos stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation to safeguard peace, stability and prosperity across Southeast Asia. He underscored the need for ASEAN member states to work together in responding to emerging regional and global challenges. Hosted by the Philippines under the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together,” the three-day summit brings together ASEAN leaders and dialogue partners to discuss key issues, including regional security, economic cooperation, maritime affairs and connectivity.India is also set to have a significant presence at the summit, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi scheduled to visit the Philippines from November 16 to 17. During his visit, Modi will participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on November 17. His participation is expected to further strengthen India’s Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with ASEAN and expand cooperation in trade, investment, maritime security and regional connectivity. The Summit is scheduled to conclude on November 17, with the Philippines set to hand over the ASEAN chairmanship to Singapore.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, today. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs. Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named player of the match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded player of the tournament.Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led India’s bowling attack, claiming four wickets.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated Team India on winning the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup. In a social media post, the President lauded the young champions for displaying exceptional skill, determination, and composure throughout the closely contested final match.Prime Minister Narendra Modi  has also congratulated the young cricketers. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today is an outstanding day for Indian cricket. He said that their success will inspire several youngsters.Congratulating young cricketers, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that the determination, firm resolve, and excellent sportsmanship they demonstrated on the pitch were a masterclass in India’s cricketing excellence.

. India’s merchandise exports rose by 45 per cent year-on-year to a record high of 49.47 billion US dollars in October this year despite the uncertainties in global markets. According to the data released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry, India’s total exports, including merchandise and services, surged by nearly 30 per cent year-on-year to reach 89.99 billion US dollars, while overall imports rose nearly 16.6 per cent to over 110 billion US dollars last month. Driven by a record merchandise export, the overall trade deficit narrowed to 20.09 billion US dollars.The Ministry noted that the major drivers of merchandise export growth in October included Petroleum Products, Electronic Goods, Gems and Jewellery, Organic and Inorganic Chemicals, and Engineering Goods. Meanwhile, India’s total exports, comprising merchandise and services, are estimated at over 568 billion dollars during April to October of the current financial year. This represents a growth of more than 16 per cent compared to the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. Government’s health expenditure has more than tripled to 4.14 lakh crore rupees in 2023-24 from 1.30 lakh crore rupees in 2013-14. This was stated in the National Health Accounts (NHA) 2023-24 report released by the Union Health Ministry.As per the report, government spending rose, increasing its overall share of total health spending by 14.9 percentage points, while per capita public healthcare expenditure nearly tripled from 1,042 to 2,959 rupees.Direct out-of-pocket expenditure by families dropped significantly by 21.5 percentage points, falling from 64.2% of total health spending down to 42.7%. Social security health spending nearly doubled from 6% to 11%, and private health insurance jumped from 3.4% to 10.2%.Primary healthcare spending reached roughly 1.53 lakh crore rupees, bolstered by programs like Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, free diagnostics, and Jan Aushadhi Kendras.

. Labour unrest in Bangladesh’s garment sector continues to disrupt industrial activities, with more than 50 factories remaining closed in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt and fresh worker protests reported in Gazipur.According to Bangladeshi media reports, garment workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail Highway in the Mouchak area of Gazipur this morning. The protest disrupted traffic for around 30 minutes after workers allegedly threw bricks at the police. Police fired tear gas to disperse the workers. Traffic movement was later restored.Meanwhile, garment industry leaders have authorised factory owners to suspend operations under the ‘no work, no pay’ provision of the Bangladesh Labour Act if unrest continues to disrupt production. The move comes as labour protests enter their third week amid demands for higher wages. Workers’ representatives on the wage board have proposed a monthly minimum wage of 32,000 taka.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached Spain’s Canary Islands by boat over the past two days, prompting fresh concerns over the growing migration crisis along the Atlantic route.According to Spain’s maritime rescue service, it assisted 1,324 people aboard 14 boats, most of whom arrived on the island of El Hierro. The number is close to the route’s daily rescue record of 1,461 migrants, set in November 2020.The Canary Islands, located off the northwest coast of Africa, remain a major entry point for migrants, particularly from West Africa, attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing in makeshift boats.According to Spain’s Interior Ministry, more than 13,000 of the over 28,000 migrants who arrived in the country by sea between January and October landed in the archipelago.Spain declared a migration emergency in the Canary Islands earlier this week following a surge in arrivals, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa.
